rows: Add the version 2 page format: the schema file with the 4 new lists (sections, stories, examples, questions for others), the changed card, note and reply shapes, the document checks that guard them, and the engine reader and newest-schema value, so `check` accepts a valid version 2 page and refuses each broken rule by name, while version 0 and 1 pages check as today.
The new format, its checks and its reader come first, because every other part reads or writes a version 2 page.

Teach ingest and the send lines the version 2 rules: a send line per ticked question for others, recorded as a signal in `questions_to_read` with no state change; a note on a section, story, example or question is a plain note owned by that element, not a session rule; a note on a settled card leaves it settled and lists it in `settled_notes_to_read`. Version 0 and 1 pages ingest as today.
Reading the send is its own cut: ticks and notes on settled points change what the agent reads, not what the page draws.

Add the page parts that draw a version 2 page's lists: a section with its current text, links, open-question chip and open change list; the questions-for-others section with its role filter control and tick inputs; the worked-examples section; and one label helper that gives every element its visible text, so no raw id or round code shows.
The new drawing parts stand alone so the plain-text rule has one label helper and one test.

Give `render` a version 2 layout beside today's, which stays untouched: title and banner with each added, merged or removed section and each change linking to its section, notes and replies on top, then the round's questions in one block with a link to each card's section, then the maps, then the sections, examples and questions for others. Write the term dictionary once on every page. Add the page-size budget test and the old-page test.
The layout, the dictionary-once rule and the size budget meet in the page shell, apart from the parts it draws.

Make the page script queue 1 answer per question for others, with its ticked option ids, replaced on each change, and add the role filter: set to a role, it shows that role's questions and the questions for everyone, in the same order, and sends nothing.
The page script holds the one external seam, the lavish checkbox check, so it gets its own cut.

Extend `build` and `apply-readings`: the 4 lists merge by id, only changed entries, each with 1 change line; `after` places a question; `section` on a card; `upgrade: true` writes a taken-over version 0 or 1 page as version 2; the builder writes the page's own version; 1 reply per note; the readings `keep`, `answer`, `drop` and `assume`.
The one writer of the page document takes every new field and reading in one place, including the upgrade the developer chose.

Move every page layout rule into use-lavish: sections, the questions block, change lists, what goes first, and the round pass for `keep`, `answer`, `drop` and `assume`; replace the rule that repeats a reply across notes with 1 reply per note that states each reading; leave visualize with pictures only; rename the glossary term Answer to Reply.
The page rules move into the page skill once the layout and the builder exist to describe.

Make grill start take over the newest finished session of the ticket and answer `takeover`; extend the end check: on a version 2 page it fails on an open question for others, a drop without reason, a story with no example and a missing example kind, and on a pass after a take-over it lists `stale` later documents and `changed` settled points. A log with no questions passes as before.
The grill's scripts change for take-over and the end check, apart from its guides, so tests prove them first.

Rewrite the grill's guides for the content: keep sections, stories, examples and questions for others in the page document; read each note for every meaning; add, order and close questions for others; propose a question on a card; print open questions as Markdown on request; come back to a finished grill with `upgrade`; ask round by round in chat without a page; and drop the page-order column, so the grill holds no layout rule.
The grill's guides come last among grill work, since they drive the scripts and point at the page rules.

Make the requirements writer's `start` answer list each assumed answer of the grill's page with who must confirm it, and make the PRD format write each as a risk, marked assumed, naming who must confirm it.
The requirements writer needs only the new format, so it can run early and alone.
